title: FOMC minutes of the October 26-27, 2027 meeting (14:00 ET) — the prose account of the year's last no-SEP decision
source: EST: the Board's own stated publication rule applied to a decision date this session read direct, then checked against the measurement a sibling lane already banked. THE RULE is verbatim from federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes, page stamp 'Last Update: August 19, 2026'): 'The minutes of regularly scheduled meetings are released three weeks after the date of the policy decision.' THE DECISION is the same page's 2027 panel, 'October 26-27' with no SEP asterisk -- Tuesday and Wednesday -- so the policy decision is Wednesday 2027-10-27 and D+21 is Wednesday 2027-11-17. THE ARITHMETIC IS NOT RE-MEASURED HERE AND THIS LANE DOES NOT CLAIM TO HAVE RE-MEASURED IT: the fomc-minutes-2027-08-18 lane parsed all 45 '(Released <Month> <D>, <YYYY>)' strings this page attaches to its own minutes links and recorded 42 of 45 at exactly D+21, every one of those a Wednesday, with the three exceptions (2023-11-01 -> 2023-11-21, 2024-11-07 -> 2024-11-26, 2025-12-10 -> 2025-12-30) all late-year releases pulled forward off a holiday week and all Tuesdays. THAT EXCEPTION CLASS IS THE ONE RISK WORTH NAMING HERE, because this is exactly a late-year release: two of the three exceptions are the November minutes of a November autumn meeting. It does not bite on these dates, and the reason is checkable -- the D+21 week here is 2027-11-15 through 2027-11-19, and the only autumn 2027 NYSE holiday is Thanksgiving 2027-11-25 (nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars, the calendar the fomc-2027-09-15 lane read at HTTP 200, 109,180 bytes, not re-fetched by this session), a full week clear. The 14:00 ET publication time is the Board's standing convention and is not stated on this page. Filed estimate because a firm rule applied to a date the Board itself calls tentative cannot be more confident than its input -- the same page states 'Each meeting date is tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it' -- so this date inherits the 2027-09-14/15 confirmation, not a better fetch. Discovered during the fomc-2027-10-26 initial research, checked 2026-09-06
notes: PROPOSED by the fomc-2027-10-26 initial research (2026-09-06), and proposed because the seeding proposal assigned it to this lane in writing: proposals/fomc-2027-10-26.from-consumer-confidence-2027-10-26.json states 'THE MINUTES ARE NOT PROPOSED HERE ... that is this meeting's lane to file rather than a CB lane's to guess -- the same precedent the 08-31 and 09-28 siblings both followed.' This is that filing. It follows the same chain fomc-2027-09-15 followed when it filed fomc-minutes-2027-10-06 on its own re-derivation; the class is already canonical in this calendar (fomc-minutes-2027-06-30.json, fomc-minutes-2027-08-18.json), so declining would leave a hole rather than hold a line. WHAT MAKES THIS PARTICULAR RELEASE WORTH TRACKING, stated narrowly because the honest answer is 'not much': 2027-10-27 is the year's LAST no-SEP decision, six weeks before the December SEP meeting that sets the 2028 dots, so these minutes are the only prose the Committee publishes between the September projections and the December ones. That is an attribution fact, not a volatility one. Impact low, and the reason is measured rather than assumed: fomc-minutes-2027-06-30's lane found the minutes channel indistinguishable from an ordinary session at n=160 (p=0.40) IN BOTH DIRECTIONS -- which refuses the trade and equally refuses treating a minutes day as a safe day. No house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates- or minutes-keyed and symbols is empty. Estimate widens caution only; nothing here licenses an entry.
